newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pac shares firm on laggards buying.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pac shares firm on laggards buying.

text.p: Strong buying interest in red-chip laggards boosted demand for CITIC Pacific Ltd, which boasts both blue and red chip credentials, brokers said.
Brokers said investors felt CITIC Pacific was cheap compared to expensive red chips, while the stock was also at a reasonable price level among other blue chips.
"Demand for red-chip laggards boosted buying for CITIC. CITIC was seriously lagging behind counterparts in the red-chip sector," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The shares were up HK$1.60 to HK$47.50 around Tuesday midday, off a high of HK$48.30 as it swam against the overall market's downtrend.

Brokers said CITIC Pacific appeared very cheap in view of its price to earnings (P/E) multiple of about 15 times, while red chips such as newly-listed Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd was trading at about 80 times P/E.
"The focus was also seen switching to CITIC following the recent surge in China Light," Mak added.
China Light, which rose 7.22 percent on Monday, added HK$0.50 or 1.20 percent to HK$42.10 on Tuesday morning. CITIC Pacific took a 20 percent stake in China Light in March.
Beijing Enterprises eased HK$2.25 to HK$52 in late morning.
